search-summaries.name: Search summaries of Decanter, Jancis Robinson and Wine With Seth on the 2019 northern Rhône
search-summaries.note: Relayed through search summaries. Those pages were not read (403, rate limits).

claims.claim: Summer was hot and very dry. Just as worry set in, enough rain came to refresh the vines and carry them to harvest. There was no disease pressure.
claims.note: One merchant report read in full. Search summaries agree on heat and dry weather.

claims.claim: A cold April brought near-frost conditions to Côte-Rôtie and Crozes-Hermitage and slowed an early budbreak.
claims.note: Relayed only. Not confirmed at source.

claims.claim: Hail on 15 June wiped out part of the Crozes-Hermitage crop. Some domaines lost up to 80%.
claims.note: Two sources agree on the June hail and Crozes. The 80% is from one. Search summaries put hail in July and include Cornas and Saint-Joseph. See conflicts.

claims.claim: August rain kept the vines out of stress but fell unevenly. Hermitage had about 50 mm, Mauves (Saint-Joseph) about 25 mm and Cornas none that day.
claims.note: JLL's figures, repeated in search summaries. Another summary mentions over 100 mm on Hermitage on 18 September. Unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Côte-Rôtie is the star. JLL calls it exceptional and says it beats 2018 across the board. Jancis Robinson's Alistair Cooper says the standout wines were in Côte-Rôtie.
claims.note: Several critics agree, through one merchant and one mirror.

claims.claim: Côte-Rôtie alcohol rose from an old norm of about 13.5% to about 14.5%. The wines stayed balanced and were called not sunstruck.
Hermitage is rated very good to exceptional. August rain helped keep the wines balanced.
claims.note: JLL's rating. Decanter is said to put Hermitage just behind Côte-Rôtie.

claims.claim: Crozes-Hermitage is uneven. Quality depends on how badly each vineyard was hit by the June hail.
Reds have ripe, substantial tannins around dense primary fruit, with fresher acidity than the heat would suggest. Many show strong ageing potential. Volumes were down in the north.
claims.note: One merchant's view, supported by quoted producers. Merchants sell the vintage.

claims.claim: The north edged the south for the merchant, but that is debated. The Rhône is seen as in the middle of a run of top years.
claims.note: Opinion of one merchant, who says time will decide.

conflicts: Hail: Laithwaites and JLL date the Crozes-Hermitage hail to 15 June. Search summaries of Jancis Robinson say July, and include Cornas, Saint-Joseph and the south of Crozes-Hermitage.
Hermitage rain: JLL gives about 50 mm in August. One search summary gives over 100 mm on 18 September. Not resolved.
Which end of the valley won: Laithwaites tips the north. Others rate the south as high.
gaps: Winter and flowering were not found.
No harvest dates or yield figures for the northern appellations.
Decanter, Jancis Robinson, Vinous and Wine With Seth pages could not be read.

sheet.vintage: 2019 was hot and dry, with just enough rain in August. Côte-Rôtie shone. Hermitage was very good too. June hail hit Crozes-Hermitage, so quality there varies.
